entry.name: mc.sfrecord~
entry.digest: Record to audio file on disk (multi-channel)
entry.description: Use the mc.sfrecord~ object to record and save multi-channel MSP output as an audio file.

arguments.name: number-of-channels
arguments.description: Sets the number of channels to record via the one multi-channel inlet. The maximum number of channels is 64, and the default is 1. The audio file created will have the same number of channels as this argument, unless you set a lower number with theattribute. Whether you can actually record the maximum number of channels is dependent on the speed of your processor and hard disk.

arguments.name: buffer-size
arguments.description: An optional second argument sets the buffer size. The defult value is 20160.

messages.name: int
messages.description: If a file has been opened with themessage, a non-zero value begins recording, andstops recording and closes the file.requires anothermessage to record again if ahas been sent.Recording may also stop spontaneously if there is an error, such as running out of space on your hard disk.

messages.name: loop
messages.digest: Trigger recording with a looping length
messages.description: If a file has been opened with themessage, the word, followed by a number that specifies the loop length in milliseconds, begins recording for the specified amount of time, repeating within the specified area.turns off recording.

messages.name: open
messages.description: In left inlet: Opens a file for recording. By default, the file type is AIFF, butalso supports WAVE, OGG, FLAC, and Raw Data. The word, without an argument, brings up a standard Save As dialog allowing you to choose a filename. The optional symbols,,,, orspecify the file format (which can also be set in the Save As dialog with a Format pop-up menu). Ifis followed by a second symbol, it creates a file in the current default volume. An existing file with the same name will be overwritten. The format symbol (e.g.,) can follow the optional filename argument. If only one argument is given to themessage, which is a filename, the file type is determined from the file extension (e.g., "open test.wav" sets the file type to).

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Output status information about recording progress
messages.description: Outputs cryptic status information about the progress of the recording.

messages.name: record
messages.digest: Record for a specified amount of time
messages.description: If a file has been opened with themessage, the word, followed by a time in milliseconds, begins recording for the specified amount of time. The recording can be stopped before it reaches the end by sendinga.

messages.name: samptype
messages.digest: Specify the sample type to use when recording
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, specifies the sample type to use when recording the audio file. The following types of sample data are supported:: 8-bit integer: 16-bit integer: 24-bit integer: 32-bit integer: 32-bit floating-point: 64-bit floating-point: 8-bit "mu"-law encoding: 8-bit a-law encodingThe optional second argument, a 0 or 1, specifies whether or not byte-swapping should be used, which is only useful when writing a 'raw' audio file.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: accepts a multi-channel signal via the one inlet, which is recorded to an audio file when recording is turned on.
